(Belleville, Illinois) | college = * [[Wright State Raiders men's basketball|Wright State]] (2018–2019) * [[Chattanooga Mocs men's basketball|Chattanooga]] (2020–2022) * [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] (2022–2023) | draft_year = 2023 | career_start = 2023 | years1 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–2024]] | team1 = [[Rip City Remix]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team2 = [[Wisconsin Herd]] | years3 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team3 = [[Memphis Hustle]] | years4 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team4 = [[Long Island Nets]] | years5 = {{nbay|2025|end}} | team5 = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | years6 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team6 = [[Toronto Raptors]] | highlights = * [[Lou Henson Award]] (2022) * [[Southern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SoCon Player of the Year]] (2022) * First-team All-[[Southern Conference|SoCon]] (2022) * First-team All-SoCon – Coaches (2021) * Second-team All-SoCon – Media (2021) * [[West Coast Conference|WCC]] Sixth Man of the Year (2023) * [[Horizon League]] All-Freshman Team (2019) }} '''Malachi Knight-Smith''' (born December 6, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Toronto Raptors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wright State Raiders men's basketball|Wright State Raiders]], [[Chattanooga Mocs men's basketball|Chattanooga Mocs]], and [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. ==High school career== Smith started playing high school basketball at [[Belleville High School-East]] in [[Belleville, Illinois]] before transferring to [[Belleville High School-West]] for his senior season.{{cite web |last1=Halfacre |first1=Paul |title=Smith has Belleville West ready for next step |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/smith-has-belleville-west-ready-for-next-step/article_93579b60-193e-11e8-a2ef-0f0891b0b072.html |website=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] |access-date=December 21, 2021 |date=February 24, 2018}} At Belleville West, he averaged 15.5 points alongside [[E. J. Liddell]] and helped his team win its first Class 4A state title.{{cite web |last1=Scott Jr. |first1=Maurice |title=Malachi Smith making his way at Wright State |url=https://www.stlamerican.com/sports/sports_columnists/from_the_east_side/malachi-smith-making-his-way-at-wright-state/article_7db6dede-357f-11e9-ba58-3fd203481cb5.html |website=[[The St. Louis American]] |access-date=December 21, 2021 |date=February 20, 2019}} Smith committed to playing college basketball for [[Wright State Raiders men's basketball|Wright State]] in November 2017, choosing the Raiders over [[Lindenwood Lions|Lindenwood]], [[Montana State Bobcats men's basketball|Montana State]] and [[Denver Pioneers men's basketball|Denver]].{{cite news |last1=Eschman |first1=Todd |title=Belleville West guard doesn’t wait for signing period to announce college choice |url=https://www.bnd.com/sports/high-school/prep-basketball/article183337546.html |access-date=December 21, 2021 |work=[[Belleville News-Democrat]] |date=November 7, 2017}} ==College career== As a freshman at [[Wright State Raiders men's basketball|Wright State]], Smith averaged 5.4 points and 2.9 rebounds per game, earning [[Horizon League]] All-Freshman Team honors. For his sophomore season, he transferred to [[Chattanooga Mocs men's basketball|Chattanooga]] and sat out for one year due to transfer rules.{{cite web |last1=Criddle |first1=Dean |title=Belleville West graduate Malachi Smith transfers to Tennessee-Chattanooga |url=https://www.bnd.com/sports/college/article231678423.html |website=[[Belleville News-Democrat]] |access-date=December 21, 2021 |date=June 19, 2019}} Smith averaged 16.8 points, 8.8 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game, earning First Team All-[[Southern Conference]] (SoCon) honors from the league's coaches, in his first year with the team.{{cite web |title=Season Review: Smith Sets New Standard |url=https://gomocs.com/news/2021/6/10/mens-basketball-season-review-smith-sets-new-standard.aspx |publisher=University of Tennessee at Chattanooga Athletics |access-date=December 21, 2021 |date=June 10, 2021}} He declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] before returning to college.{{cite web |last1=Nyman |first1=Rick |title=Mocs Malachi Smith and David Jean Baptiste Enjoyed NBA Draft Process |url=https://www.wdef.com/mocs-malachi-smith-david-jean-baptiste-enjoyed-nba-draft-process/ |publisher=[[WDEF-TV]] |access-date=December 21, 2021 |date=July 8, 2021}} On November 18, 2021, he scored a career-high 36 points in an 87–76 loss to [[Murray State Racers men's basketball|Murray State]].{{cite web |title=Brown carries Murray State past Chattanooga 87-76 |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2021/12/18/brown-carries-murray-state-past-chattanooga-87-76/49546901/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=December 21, 2021 |date=December 18, 2021}} At the close of his sophomore season, Smith was named the [[Southern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Southern Conference Player of the Year]] by both the league's coaches and media.{{cite press release|url=https://soconsports.com/news/2022/3/2/all-socon-mens-basketball-teams-announced.aspx|title=All-SoCon men's basketball teams announced|publisher=[[Southern Conference]]|date=March 2, 2022|access-date=March 2, 2022|archive-date=March 2, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220302210037/https://soconsports.com/news/2022/3/2/all-socon-mens-basketball-teams-announced.aspx|url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== ===Rip City Remix (2023–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Smith joined the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Announce NBA 2K24 NBA Summer League 2023 Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-announce-nba-2k24-nba-summer-league-2023-roster|website=NBA.com|date=June 30, 2023|access-date=October 4, 2023}} and on October 2, 2023, he signed with them.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Five Players|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-five-players|website=NBA.com|date=October 2, 2023|access-date=October 4, 2023}} However, he was waived on October 10{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign George Conditt|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-george-conditt|website=NBA.com|date=October 10, 2023|access-date=October 11, 2023}} and on October 30, he joined the [[Rip City Remix]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite tweet|first=Casey|last=Holdahl|title=The @ripcityremix begin training camp for their {{as written|ina|gural [sic]}} season today at the @trailblazers practice facility. Here's who they're taking into camp...|number=1719017456981696590|user=CHold|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=November 12, 2023}} ===Wisconsin Herd (2024)=== On January 12, 2024, Smith was traded to the [[Wisconsin Herd]] in exchange for [[Jazian Gortman]].{{cite web|title=WISCONSIN HERD ACQUIRE MALACHI SMITH|url=https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-acquire-malachi-smith|website=NBA.com|date=January 12, 2024|access-date=January 16, 2024}} He made 27 appearances (including six starts) for the Herd, recording averages of 9.5 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 2.7 assists. ===Memphis Hustle (2024–2025)=== On October 9, 2024, Smith was traded to the [[Memphis Hustle]].{{cite web|title=Memphis Hustle complete six-team trade|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-complete-six-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=October 9, 2024|access-date=October 9, 2024}} He made 31 appearances (including eight starts) for Memphis during the [[2024–25 NBA G League season]], averaging 11.4 points, 4.0 rebounds, and 2.8 assists. ===Long Island / Brooklyn Nets (2025–2026)=== On September 9, 2025, Smith was traded to the [[Long Island Nets]] in exchange for [[Jordan Minor]] and a 2026 first-round pick.{{Cite web |date=September 9, 2025 |title=Long Island Nets Acquire Malachi Smith From The Memphis Hustle |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DOZcHZmkTg_/?igsh=cXR3bjV0bmE0ZWZn}} On March 13, 2026, Smith signed a 10-day contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{Cite web|title=Nets' Malachi Smith: Signs with Nets|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/nets-malachi-smith-signs-with-nets/|access-date=March 14, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}{{Cite web|title=Malachi Smith earns Nets 10-day contract as Grant Nelson's season ends early|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/malachi-smith-earns-nets-10-183259302.html|access-date=March 16, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}} He signed a second 10-day contract with Brooklyn on March 24.https://gleague.nba.com/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-malachi-smith-to-second-10-day-contract On April 4, following the expiration of his 10-day deal, Brooklyn re-signed Smith to a two-year, standard NBA contract.{{Cite web|title=Nets reward Malachi Smith with two-year contract after ‘anything but easy’ journey to NBA|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/nets-reward-malachi-smith-two-153940022.html|access-date=June 11, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}} On April 10, he recorded 19 points, 10 assists, and eight rebounds in a 108–125 loss to the [[2025–26 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web|title=Nets Exercise Smith's Team Option for 2026-27 Season|url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/nets-exercise-smith-team-option-174054508.html|access-date=June 29, 2026|website=ca.sports.yahoo.com|language=en}} In total, Smith appeared in ten [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] regular-season games, averaging 7.3 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 2.0 assists. On July 10, Smith was waived by the Nets.{{Cite web|title=Malachi Smith: Waived by Brooklyn|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/malachi-smith-waived-by-brooklyn-531655/|access-date=August 13, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} ===Toronto Raptors (2026–present)=== On August 17, 2026, Smith signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|title=Raptors sign Smith|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-smith |website=NBA.com|date=August
